the evolutionary history of the melanophore receptors for MCH and MSH, and with their role in the physiological color change of fishes.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the evolution of the MCH-MCH receptor system occurred in the lineage ancestral to the teleosts and was not present in the lineage ancestral either to the chondrosteans or to the holosteans.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
MCH receptors were lost in the chondrostean lineage but were retained in the lineage ancestral to neopterygians.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the melanophore receptor for MCH evolved before the evolution of teleosts.
the MCH receptor is not a universal component of melanophores in bony fishes, but is present in the melanophores of some, but not all species of neopterygii.
the melanophore receptor for MCH is a useful marker to trace the evolution of the melanosome aggregation-dispersion mechanism in the integument of ray-finned fishes.
